content:
- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates or overshoots after sharp moves; cap upward spikes and adjust downward if sentiment turns negative.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), leading to overshoots in 10-15 day forecasts; apply smoothing or lag correction for such periods.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; introduce a “sentiment pivot” rule: if sentiment drops below 0.33 after 7-10 days, reduce forecast by 1-2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10-15 day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 0.5-1.0% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often ignores sentiment trend; if sentiment is trending upward, add 0.5-1.5% buffer to forecast; if trending downward, subtract 0.5-1.5%.
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes (e.g., 1.00) are common in 10-20 day horizon; apply “sentiment decay” rule: reduce forecast by 0.2-0.5% per day after sentiment peak.
